mainTopic: Who is believed about blemishes on a בכור and on מעשר, and when three ordinary people may permit a blemished בכור.
overview: This amud deals with who is believed about blemishes on holy animals. First the גמרא finishes testing רב's rule that a כהן is believed when he says a ישראל gave him a בכור that was already blemished. It tries to prove the rule from a משנה about a שליח buying produce, but the proof is turned away. רבי ירמיה בר אבא then says the tradition got changed along the way: really it is the ישראל who is believed. The הלכה follows even the first, more lenient version, and the story of רפרם shows that one brazen כהן does not make all כהנים suspect. רב אשי rules that a בכור born with an obvious blemish may be examined even without a כהן present. A new משנה says that anyone, even the owner, is believed about blemishes on a מעשר animal, because he could have blemished his whole flock beforehand. Another משנה lets three ordinary people permit a בכור with an obvious blemish, while רבי יוסי requires an expert. The גמרא limits this to obvious blemishes and to a place with no expert, and begins discussing רב חייא בר עמרם's parallel rule about undoing a נדר. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The agent can easily wriggle out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting a proof from the first half of the משנה. The שליח there may lie because he has an easy excuse ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because he has a way to get himself out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rejection that started just before this. The שליח in the first half of the משנה is not believed because he can always slip out of blame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first half of the משנה, the שליח was told to buy from 'someone trustworthy,' and he says he did. If caught, he can simply claim he thought that seller was trustworthy, so he is not afraid to lie. That is why this case cannot disprove רב's rule that people do not lie about things that can be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: to slip away, to wriggle out of an accusation

phrases.english: since he has a way to slip out of it.
phrases.notes: He can say, 'I really thought that seller was trustworthy.' Nobody can prove him wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection, begun before this section, of the challenge from the first half of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the first half of the משנה against רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שליח there has an easy excuse that cannot be checked, so his case is not one where a lie would surely come out.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה seems to support רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the second half of the same משנה as clear support for רב. There, a שליח sent to a specific named seller is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second half of the משנה surely supports him: if he was told 'from so-and-so,' he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tries to prove רב's rule from the second half of the same משנה. In that half, a שליח sent to buy from one named person is believed when he says he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the seller is a specific known person, so the story can easily be checked by asking him. The שליח is believed because people do not lie when they can be caught. That looks exactly like רב's reasoning.

phrases.english: The latter clause certainly supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב, whose rule is that people don't lie about things that can be found out.

phrases.english: 'From so-and-so' — this one is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the משנה (which was not a problem for רב) to the second half, offered as positive support.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a person does not lie about a matter that can be checked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the משנה in דמאי: a שליח sent to a named seller is believed.

steps.title: There, someone may come to check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the משנה, the person who sent the שליח named the seller, so the שליח expects to be checked and is afraid to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since he has someone who will demand an answer, he is afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The case in the משנה is different from רב's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the sender himself named the seller, so the שליח assumes the sender plans to check, and that makes him afraid to lie. In רב's case, the כהן brings up the ישראל on his own and nobody is planning to check. So the כהן might not be afraid, and the משנה does not prove רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: a claimant, someone who will demand an answer

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב is wrong. It only says this משנה cannot serve as proof for him.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ תּוֹבֵעַ, מִירְתַת.
phrases.english: There, since he has a claimant, he is afraid.
phrases.notes: The 'claimant' is the person who sent him and named the seller. The שליח assumes he will check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the second half of the משנה as support for רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה there is a person who intends to check, which makes the שליח afraid to lie. That is not true in רב's case.

steps.title: The tradition was passed on wrong: the ישראל is the one believed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says that רב יהודה received the teaching wrongly through גידול. The real version is that a ישראל is believed to say he gave the בכור to a כהן already blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: Where did יהודה get this from? I taught it to גידול, and גידול taught it to him. But this is what I actually said to him: a ישראל is believed to say, 'I gave this בכור to a כהן with its מום.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא challenges the very wording of רב יהודה's report. He says it got mixed up along the way, and he gives the correct version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה had said the כהן is believed about a ישראל having given him a blemished בכור. רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the teaching passed from him to גידול and then to רב יהודה, and it was changed along the way. In the real version, the ישראל is believed to say he gave it to the כהן with its מום already there. The person speaking switches from the כהן to the ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: I taught it, I fixed it (as a set teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Two attempted proofs for רב from the משנה about a שליח were both turned away. Then רבי ירמיה בר אבא fixed the tradition itself: the ישראל is believed that he gave the בכור already blemished, not the כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Who is believed matters in practice. A blemished בכור may be slaughtered and eaten, so it makes a real difference whose word we accept that the מום was not made deliberately.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
From where does Yehuda have this?
phrases.notes: 'Yehuda' is רב יהודה, who reported the rule about the כהן in רב's name.

phrases.english: I taught it to Giddul,
and Giddul taught it to him.
And this is what I said to him:
A Yisrael is believed to say,
'I gave this firstborn to a Kohen with its blemish.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: מְנָא לֵיהּ לִיהוּדָה הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the search for proofs and goes back to question the exact wording of רב יהודה's report in the name of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the correct version of רב's teaching, a ישראל is believed to say he gave the בכור to a כהן already blemished.

steps.title: Why would we need to say a ישראל is believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה בר אבא's version: of course a ישראל is believed, since he gains nothing from the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the version of רבי ירמיה בר אבא from Step 4. Why teach that a ישראל is believed, when that seems obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל who already gave the בכור away gets nothing from saying it had a מום. He has no reason to lie, so a rule that he is believed seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
A regular Jew who is not a כהן; here, the one who gave the בכור

phrases.english: An Israelite? It is obvious!
phrases.notes: He has nothing to gain, since the animal already belongs to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the teaching given in Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's version that a ישראל is believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person with no gain has no reason to lie, so the rule seems unnecessary

steps.title: The animal was young and then grew up
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a case where the animal was small when given and grew bigger since, so we might think the ישראל can't recognize it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where it was young and grew up. You might have said he does not recognize it for sure. So it teaches us that he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The question is not whether the ישראל is honest, but whether he can really recognize the animal after it changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that grew up looks different. We might fear the ישראל is honestly mixing it up with another בכור that the כהן blemished on purpose. The rule teaches that we trust him to recognize it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a special case)
It was young and then grew up
He does not know it for sure
So it teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: The worry here is not that the ישראל is lying. The worry is that he is honestly mistaken because the animal looks different now.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for when it was young and grew up,
you might have said: he does not recognize it for sure?
So it teaches us (that he is believed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the animal grew and changed, the ישראל may not truly recognize it
steps.terutzMaskana: The ישראל is trusted to recognize the animal he gave

steps.title: How סורא and פומבדיתא taught it, and the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: סורא taught the second version (a ישראל is believed); פומבדיתא taught the first version (even a כהן is believed). The הלכה follows even the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught like the later version. In פומבדיתא they taught like the first version. And the הלכה is even like the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports which version each yeshiva used and then gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version, from רב יהודה in the name of רב, is more lenient: even the כהן himself is believed. The הלכה follows that version, so a כהן is believed too, and certainly a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version (רב יהודה: even a כהן is believed)
The later version (רבי ירמיה בר אבא: a ישראל is believed)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that even a כהן is believed to say a ישראל gave him the בכור already blemished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole discussion about who is believed.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught like the latter version,
in Pumbedita like the first version,
and the halakha is even like the first version.
phrases.notes: "Even" means the more lenient version: the כהן himself is also believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions discussed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the first, more lenient version: even a כהן is believed

steps.title: The story of רפרם and the dishonest כהן
steps.stepSummary: רפרם gave an unblemished בכור to a כהן, who blemished it and later brought it to רפרם claiming a ישראל gave it to him blemished. רפרם recognized it as his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם in פומבדיתא had a בכור and gave it to a כהן without a מום. The כהן went and put a מום on it. One day רפרם's eyes were weak, and the כהן brought the animal before him. He said: A ישראל gave me this בכור with its מום. רפרם forced his eyes open, saw it, and recognized it. He said: Wasn't I the one who gave it to you?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story connected to the rule that a כהן is believed. It sets up the lesson that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a כהן actually lied, using exactly the claim the הלכה believes. He picked a day when רפרם could barely see, but רפרם opened his eyes and caught him. This raises the question of whether כהנים should still be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish, which lets a בכור be eaten outside the בית המקדש
He put a blemish on it on purpose (which is forbidden)

phrases.english: Rafram in Pumbedita had a firstborn animal,
and he gave it to a priest without a blemish.
He (the priest) went and put a blemish on it.
One day he (Rafram) was weak in his eyes,
he (the priest) brought it before him.
phrases.notes: He brought it so רפרם, as an expert, would check the blemish and allow it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּכוֹר זֶה נָתַן לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: This firstborn was given to me
by an Israelite with its blemish.
He forced his eyes open,
saw it, and recognized it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו אֲנָא דִּיהֵיבְתֵּיהּ לָךְ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Wasn't I the one who gave it to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that tests the ruling that a כהן is believed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real case where a כהן falsely claimed a ישראל gave him a blemished בכור

steps.title: One bold liar does not make all כהנים suspect
steps.stepSummary: Even after catching the כהן, רפרם was not worried about other כהנים, since only this one was so brazen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, he was not worried about the matter. This one is brazen; everyone else is not brazen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story with its lesson. The ruling that a כהן is believed still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This כהן was unusually bold, bringing the animal to the very person who gave it to him. One extreme case does not prove that כהנים in general lie, so the lenient הלכה from Step 7 is not changed.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not worried about the matter

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה stays: a כהן is believed. A single brazen liar is the exception, not proof that everyone lies.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא חַשׁ לַהּ לְמִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: And even so, he was not concerned about the matter,
this one is the one who is brazen,
everyone else is not brazen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא חַשׁ לַהּ לְמִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the רפרם story
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One brazen כהן's lie does not undo the rule that כהנים are believed

steps.title: רב אשי: an inborn, obvious blemish raises no worry
steps.stepSummary: A בכור that was a שָׂרוּעַ came before רב אשי. He said there is nothing to worry about, whether a כהן or a ישראל brought it, because the blemish came naturally with the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain שָׂרוּעַ animal was brought before רב אשי. He said: what should we worry about? Whether it is a כהן or a ישראל, this is a בכור whose blemish came with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. A בכור with one eye bigger than the other was brought to רב אשי, and he said there is no reason for concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps worried that someone might make a blemish on purpose. This blemish is clearly from birth, so nobody could have caused it. That means it should not matter who brought the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with one limb bigger than the other; here, one eye larger than the other
What should we be worried about?
Its blemish is with it, meaning it was born with it

phrases.english: A certain animal with one eye larger than the other
phrases.notes: שָׂרוּעַ literally means 'stretched out.' Here it means a בכור with one eye bigger than the other.

phrases.english: that came before Rav Ashi,
he said: What should we be concerned about with it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כֹּהֵן הוּא, אִי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
phrases.english: Whether it is a priest or whether it is an Israelite
this is a firstborn whose blemish is with it.
phrases.notes: He means the animal was born this way, so nobody could have made the blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שָׂרוּעַ דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case. It contrasts with the רפרם story, where the blemish was made on purpose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור with an obvious, inborn blemish may be examined no matter who brings it.

steps.title: רבינא: רב יהודה requires a כהן to be present
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects: perhaps a ישראל brought it, and רב יהודה said a ישראל's בכור is not examined unless a כהן is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But maybe it is a ישראל, and רב יהודה said we do not examine a ישראל's בכור unless a כהן is with him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's statement that it does not matter who brought the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי only looked at the worry that the blemish was made on purpose. רבינא points to a different rule. According to רב יהודה, a ישראל's בכור needs a כהן present at the examination, even if the blemish is not in doubt.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps it is an Israelite,
and Rav Yehuda said:
One may not examine the firstborn of an Israelite
unless a priest is with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְדִלְמָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's claim that the bringer's identity does not matter.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's statement 'אי כהן הוא אי ישראל הוא'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה's rule requires a כהן to be present for a ישראל's בכור, so the identity of the bringer does matter.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב יהודה's worry is stealing from the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the cases are different. In רב יהודה's case, the ישראל would not eat the בכור without checking, but he is suspected of taking the כהן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare? There, even though he will not eat קדשים outside, he is suspected about the כהן's money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins his answer by explaining the reason behind רב יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל will not risk the serious sin of eating קדשים outside, so he will have the blemish checked. However, once the animal is allowed, he might keep it instead of giving it to the כהן. That is why רב יהודה wants a כהן there.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred meat eaten outside its allowed place or status

phrases.english: He said to him: How can these be compared?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, נְהִי דְּקָדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָא אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: There, granted that he will not eat sacred meat outside,
he is suspected regarding the priest's property.
phrases.notes: The worry is that after the animal is allowed, the ישראל keeps it instead of giving it to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבינא by explaining the reason for רב יהודה's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's rule applies to every ישראל's בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה's rule is based on the fear that the ישראל will take the כהן's property. The next step shows why that fear does not apply here.

steps.title: Here the owner came only out of respect, so he can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: Here the blemish is obvious, so the owner did not need a חכם. He came only out of respect for the חכם, and someone who honors a חכם will not commit a sin like stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, since he knows this is a clear blemish, why did he bring it before the רבנן? Out of respect for the חכם. He does not neglect the honor of a חכם, and he would commit a sin?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer by explaining why the worry about stealing does not apply in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an obvious blemish, the ישראל could have decided by himself that the animal is allowed. The fact that he still came to a חכם shows he is careful about כבוד חכמים. Such a person can be trusted to give the animal to the כהן, so no כהן needs to be present.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor due to a Torah scholar

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה requires a כהן to be present only because a ישראל might keep the כהן's בכור. When the blemish is obvious and the owner still comes to a חכם out of respect, we trust him, and no כהן is needed.

phrases.english: Here, since he knows
that this is a clear-cut blemish,
why did he bring it before the Sages?
Because of the honor of the Sage;
he does not go against the honor of a Sage,
and he would commit a transgression?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא, מִכְּדֵי יָדַע דְּהַאי מוּם מוּבְהָק הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's distinction by showing the stealing worry does not apply to an obvious blemish.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ישראל who brings a בכור might keep it for himself, so a כהן must be present.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing an obvious blemish to a חכם shows that the owner can be trusted, so רב אשי's ruling stands.

steps.title: Everyone is trusted about blemishes on a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that anyone, even the owner, is believed when he says a מעשר animal has a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone is believed about the blemishes of a מעשר animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that anyone, including the owner, is trusted to say a מעשר בהמה animal is blemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the worry with a בכור was that someone with a stake in it might have caused the blemish or misreport it. Here the משנה gives a much easier rule for מעשר. Even the person who gains from the ruling is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe: every tenth animal of the flock becomes holy

phrases.english: MISHNA: Everyone is believed
phrases.notes: "Everyone" here includes the owner himself, even though he gains if the animal is ruled blemished.

phrases.english: about the blemishes of a tithe animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It contrasts with the concern, discussed for a בכור, that an interested party might have made or misreported a blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone, even the owner, is trusted about blemishes on a מעשר animal.

steps.title: Why is the owner trusted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's lenient rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the owner is believed, since he gains from his own testimony. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person who benefits from a ruling is not trusted about it. So the גמרא needs a reason why מעשר is different.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the owner, who benefits, is believed about blemishes on a מעשר animal.

steps.title: He could have blemished it from the start
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the owner could have legally blemished the animal before it became מעשר, so he has no reason to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he wanted, he could have put a blemish on it from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner had a legal way to get the same result. He could have blemished the animal before it became holy, so there is no reason to suspect him now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before an animal becomes מעשר, it is ordinary and may be blemished. Someone who could have gotten the result legally is not suspected of lying to get it.

phrases.english: Because if he wanted,
he could have put a blemish on it from the beginning!
phrases.notes: "From the beginning" means before the animal became holy as מעשר, when blemishing it was still allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner could have legally blemished this animal before it became מעשר, so he has no reason to lie.

steps.title: Nobody knows which animal will come out tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the owner cannot know ahead of time which animal will be the tenth, and the תורה forbids him from arranging it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he know which one will come out tenth? And if you say he sends a chosen animal out as the tenth, the תורה says "He shall not search whether it be good or bad"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 16. The owner cannot blemish "this animal" beforehand, because he does not know which one will end up as מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals pass through a gate one by one, and whichever comes out tenth becomes מעשר. You might think the owner could steer a chosen animal into the tenth spot. But the פסוק forbids picking, so the animals must come out on their own. That means the owner never knew which animal to blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the ten, meaning the tenth animal
He shall not search or choose (ויקרא 27:33)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Does he know which one will come out?
phrases.notes: He means: which animal will walk out tenth and become מעשר.

phrases.english: And if you say he sends it out
as the head of the ten,
"He shall not search whether it be good or bad"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33

phrases.english: the Merciful One said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 16, and blocks a possible defense ahead of time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner could have blemished this particular animal beforehand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody knows in advance which animal will be tenth. Choosing the tenth animal on purpose is forbidden by the פסוק, so blemishing that specific animal in advance was never possible.

steps.title: He could have blemished his whole flock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the answer: the owner could have legally blemished every animal in his flock, so he is still not suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if he wanted, he could have put a blemish on his entire flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the same basic idea but makes it bigger. The owner could have blemished all his animals before tithing, so whichever one came out tenth would be blemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in Step 17 was not knowing which animal would be tenth. Blemishing the whole flock solves that. Since the owner always had a legal way to get a blemished מעשר, he has no reason to lie, so he is believed.
steps.whatToRemember: The owner is believed about blemishes on מעשר because he could have legally blemished his whole flock before tithing.

phrases.english: Rather, because if he wanted,
he could have put a blemish
on his entire flock.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the spelling in round brackets; the one in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "his entire."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 by restating the reason of Step 16 more broadly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner could have blemished this specific animal beforehand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner could have blemished his whole flock beforehand, so he is not suspected about any animal.

steps.title: Obvious blemishes on a בכור: three ordinary people are enough
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a בכור with an obvious blemish may be slaughtered based on three ordinary people from the synagogue.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בכור whose eye was blinded, or whose foreleg was cut off, or whose hind leg was broken may be slaughtered on the word of three people of the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a בכור with very obvious blemishes. It rules that no expert is needed, and three ordinary people may permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a בכור needs an expert to rule that its blemish is a real, permanent one. A blinded eye or a cut-off or broken leg is plain to anyone. That is why this משנה says three regular people can decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, given to a כהן
Ordinary people who attend the synagogue

phrases.english: MISHNA: A firstborn whose eye was blinded,
or whose foreleg was cut off,
phrases.notes: For an animal, "hand" means a front leg.

phrases.english: or whose hind leg was broken —
this may be slaughtered
on the word of three people of the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר שֶׁנִּסְמֵית עֵינוֹ וְשֶׁנִּקְטְעָה יָדוֹ וְשֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה רַגְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about who may rule on a בכור's blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור with an obvious blemish may be slaughtered based on three ordinary people, without an expert.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only an expert may permit it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees: even a court of twenty-three is not enough, and only an expert may permit the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even if twenty-three are there, it may be slaughtered only on the word of an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He says that even for an obvious blemish, only an expert can permit slaughtering a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion, an obvious blemish needs no special skill. רבי יוסי holds that permitting a בכור always needs an expert. Even a large court of twenty-three judges does not replace one.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-three, the size of a בית דין that judges capital cases
Expert, here an expert in judging blemishes

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא allows three ordinary people to permit a בכור with an obvious blemish. רבי יוסי requires an expert no matter how many people are present.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if there are twenty-three there,
phrases.notes: He means even a full court of twenty-three judges.

phrases.english: it is not slaughtered
except on the word of an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה (Step 19).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור may be slaughtered only on the ruling of an expert, even if the blemish is obvious and many people are present.

steps.title: Three synagogue members may permit a בכור outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי and others teach that outside ארץ ישראל, a בכור may be permitted by three ordinary people from the synagogue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי and רבי יהודה נשיאה both say in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי (and some say רבי שמלאי and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה): permitting a בכור outside ארץ ישראל can be done by three people from the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a teaching: outside ארץ ישראל, three ordinary people can declare a בכור blemished and permit it to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who said it in whose name, but the rule itself is the same. Outside ארץ ישראל a בכור can never be brought as a קרבן, so the rule is more relaxed and does not demand an expert.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitting a firstborn animal to be slaughtered and eaten because of a blemish
Ordinary people who come to the synagogue, not experts

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Simlai and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי
phrases.english: both say in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: and some say: Rabbi Simlai and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה אָמְרִי
phrases.english: both say in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
The permitting of a firstborn outside the Land
is by three members of the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה from step 19 about three synagogue members.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside ארץ ישראל, three ordinary synagogue members may permit a בכור.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to obvious blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that the three synagogue members may only permit a בכור with clear, obvious blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and only with obvious blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule just taught: it only applies when the blemish is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even outside ארץ ישראל, non-experts can only rule on blemishes anyone can see. A blemish that needs skill to judge still needs an expert.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious, clear-cut blemishes that anyone can recognize

phrases.english: Rava said:
And with obvious blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three synagogue members can only permit a בכור whose blemish is obvious.

steps.title: Why does רבא need to say this if the משנה already says it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא adds, since the משנה already lists obvious blemishes for the three synagogue members.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבא teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: a בכור whose eye was blinded, whose foreleg was cut off, or whose hind leg was broken may be slaughtered based on three synagogue members!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה already gives only obvious blemishes as examples, so his statement seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blinded eye, a cut-off leg and a broken leg are all obvious blemishes. Since the משנה lists only these, it seems clear the rule is about obvious blemishes, so what is new in רבא's words?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what is new in a statement)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: a firstborn whose eye was blinded
phrases.notes: This is the משנה we saw in step 19.

phrases.english: and whose foreleg was cut off, and whose hind leg was broken —
this one may be slaughtered
by three members of the synagogue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in step 22 as already known.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already lists only obvious blemishes, so רבא's statement adds nothing.

steps.title: Without רבא, we might think the משנה allows even unclear blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from the משנה alone we might think obvious blemishes were chosen only to show how strict רבי יוסי is, so רבא is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said: outside ארץ ישראל, even blemishes that are not obvious are allowed, and the reason the משנה mentions obvious blemishes is to show how far רבי יוסי goes. So רבא teaches us that it is only obvious blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's statement is needed: the משנה could have been read in a broader way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the משנה used obvious blemishes only to show that רבי יוסי demands an expert even for those, while the first opinion allows even unclear ones. רבא tells us no: the three synagogue members can only permit obvious blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a possible mistaken reading)
To show you how far someone's opinion goes

steps.whatToRemember: Three ordinary synagogue members may permit a בכור only when the blemish is obvious. An unclear blemish always needs an expert.

phrases.english: If from the Mishnah alone, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ אֲפִילּוּ מוּמִין שֶׁאֵין מוּבְהָקִין,
phrases.english: outside the Land, even blemishes that are not obvious,
and the fact that it teaches obvious ones —
is to show you how far Rabbi Yosei goes,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי (step 20) wants an expert even for an obvious blemish; that is how strict he is.

phrases.english: so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the earlier source could be read in a broader way, so the new statement is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions obvious blemishes only to show רבי יוסי's strictness, while the first opinion allows even unclear blemishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three synagogue members may only permit obvious blemishes.

steps.title: Three people may permit a בכור where there is no expert
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, citing רבי ירמיה בר אבא in the name of either רב or שמואל, teaches that three people may permit a בכור where no expert is available.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רבי ירמיה בר אבא said, perhaps in the name of רב, perhaps in the name of שמואל: three people may permit a בכור in a place where there is no expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: where there is no expert, three ordinary people may permit a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The speaker was not sure whether the teaching came from רב or from שמואל, but the rule itself is clear. It sets up the next question, which asks what is new about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Unsure whether it was said in the name of this person

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב, סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: perhaps in the name of Rav, perhaps in the name of Shmuel:
Three may permit the firstborn
in a place where there is no expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same topic of three people permitting a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where there is no expert, three people may permit a בכור.

steps.title: Why does רב יהודה need to say this if the משנה already says it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יהודה adds, since the משנה already says three synagogue members may permit a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: this one may be slaughtered by three members of the synagogue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's teaching: it seems to repeat what the משנה already says. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already allows three synagogue members to permit a בכור, so a rule that three people may permit it seems to add nothing. This is the same kind of question asked about רבא in step 23.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: this one may be slaughtered
by three members of the synagogue!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא: הֲרֵי זֶה יִשָּׁחֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's teaching in step 25 as already known from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that three may permit a בכור where there is no expert
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says three synagogue members may permit a בכור, so the teaching seems to add nothing.

steps.title: רב יהודה limits the rule to a place with no expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה alone might suggest three people can permit a בכור even where an expert is available. רב יהודה teaches that they may do so only where there is no expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said that three people may permit a בכור even where there is an expert. So רב יהודה teaches us: where there is no expert, yes; where there is an expert, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 26 about what רב יהודה adds to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says three synagogue members may permit a בכור, but it does not say when. Without רב יהודה, we might think this works even if an expert is nearby. רב יהודה adds the limit: three people may decide only when no expert is available.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (what we might have wrongly thought)

steps.whatToRemember: Three ordinary people may permit a בכור only where there is no expert. If an expert is available, they must use him.

phrases.english: If it were only from the משנה, I would have said:
even in a place where there is an expert,
phrases.notes: The word "even" is not written, but the גמרא means it: three people could decide even with an expert around.

phrases.english: so he teaches us:
in a place where there is no expert, yes,
in a place where there is an expert, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the statement adds a limit the משנה left unclear
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three people may permit a בכור even where an expert is available.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three people may permit a בכור only where no expert is available.

steps.title: Three may permit a firstborn or undo a vow when no expert is present
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר עמרם teaches two parallel rules: three people may permit a בכור where there is no expert, and three people may undo a נדר where there is no חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר עמרם said: Three people may permit a בכור in a place where there is no expert. Three people may undo a נדר in a place where there is no חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב חייא בר עמרם, gives a statement with two matching halves, one about a בכור and one about a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves follow the same pattern: when the usual single authority (an expert for blemishes, a חכם for vows) is missing, a group of three people can take his place. The גמרא will now look at each half separately.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn animal, which may be eaten only if it has a blemish
a Torah scholar who can undo a vow by himself

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Amram said:
Three people may permit the firstborn animal
in a place where there is no expert;
three people may undo a vow
in a place where there is no Sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on the same topic of three people permitting a בכור, now paired with undoing a נדר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where the usual authority is missing, three people may permit a בכור (no expert) or undo a נדר (no חכם).

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the firstborn half again to examine it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the first half of רב חייא בר עמרם's statement, about permitting a בכור, so it can discuss it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three people may permit a בכור in a place where there is no expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first half of רב חייא בר עמרם's words again. It is setting up the next move, a discussion of this half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half matches what רב יהודה already taught in steps 25-27. The גמרא quotes it again so it can explain each half of רב חייא בר עמרם's statement in turn. That explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: in a place where there is no

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is repeating words it just quoted so it can discuss them.

phrases.english: Three people may permit the firstborn animal
in a place where there is no expert
phrases.notes: This repeats the first half of the statement in step 28, so the גמרא can explain it; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַתִּירִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the first half of step 28 to begin examining it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The גמרא quotes the בכור half of רב חייא בר עמרם's statement so it can explain it; the explanation continues on the next amud.
